text: Fodor's modularity thesis holds that the central systems responsible for reasoning and belief fixation are modular in the same way that perceptual input systems are.
explanation: False. Fodor's thesis is precisely that input systems are modular (domain-specific, encapsulated, fast, mandatory) while central systems are NOT modular -- they are isotropic and holistic. The view that modularity goes 'all the way up' is the rival massive-modularity thesis (Sperber, Cosmides, Tooby), which Fodor rejected.
